facts.claim: A significant positive relationship between the amount of online communication and perceptions of relational messages (intimacy, composure, informality, social orientation), forecasts of the future of the relationship, and information seeking behavior when meeting their partner FtF was found to be curvilinear.
facts.quote: Results were consistent with the hypothesized curvilinear relationship between the amount of online communication and perceptions of relational messages (intimacy, composure, informality, social orientation), forecasts of the future of the relationship, and information seeking behavior when meeting their partner FtF.

facts.claim: Over 85% (n = 19) of studies reported a significant negative impact of dating app use on body image.
facts.quote: Over 85% (n = 19) of studies reported a significant negative impact of dating app use on body image, and 48. 6% (n = 14) of studies reported significant negative impacts on mental health and wellbeing.

research.angle: While online dating is linked to negative impacts on body image and mental health, the success of these relationships depends on specific communication strategies and the amount of online interaction before meeting offline.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that online dating has specific psychological risks and that relationship outcomes are influenced by communication patterns rather than being simply similar to offline dating.
research.caveat: The sources do not provide a direct comparison of overall relationship success rates between online and offline couples.
